correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Cayley action, exact vertex labels and fifteen edge transpositions. Verified state-by-state breadth-first search over all 10! placements in two distinct programs (factoradic indexing and 40-bit hashed encodings), using each exact package source and a cross-check script. The complete eighteen-layer counts and four extremizer strings agree; all 3,628,800 states are visited. Since every graph edge is enumerated, BFS layers equal shortest distances, not experimental upper bounds. Every swap reduces total ground-distance by at most 2, giving the transported ceiling-half bound; both programs find gap maximum 4 on 1,440 states. Directly replayed a 17-swap path to one antipode. Transitive token relabelling transfers these exact results to all initial placements. The finite scope and nonproof of any all-size conjecture are explicit.

value.rationale: The pentagonal prism is a canonical odd circular ladder and a natural ten-node cubic interconnection network. Its complete 10!-state shortest-swap profile, the geometric four-antipode classification, and the exact count of failures of the standard transport lower bound form a substantive, reproducible benchmark. Unlike a routine example of general BFS, the requested unknowns are specific motivated network invariants, and the sharp extremal configurations have simple structural meaning. The result is deliberately finite, rather than claiming an unwarranted extension.
